recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is -0.3% vs baseline (64.1 vs 64.3 ms), with latest reading at 69.0 — a rebound but still below trend
Sleep is chronically insufficient: 15 nights <7h in last 14 days, recent avg 4.5h (baseline 4.5h) — no improvement despite high load
Training readiness avg 7d is 34.9 (very low); latest is 57 — partial rebound but remains sub-threshold for quality work
Recovery balance is 2.55 (positive), yet acute:chronic workload ratio (ACWR) is only 0.6 — indicating significant underloading due to fatigue, not intentional recovery
Resting HR improved (-0.7 bpm), but this reflects detraining adaptation rather than true recovery resilience
readiness.guidance: The athlete is fatigued and sleep-deprived; the body is conserving resources — prioritize sleep restoration and low-intensity movement over performance targets.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows markedly reduced volume and intensity versus last month, with slower average pace, lower zone 3–4 time, and elevated aerobic TE — consistent with fatigue-driven pacing and reduced neuromuscular efficiency.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +34 spm this month (152 vs 118), likely reflecting forced short-stride compensation on fatigued legs — not improved technique — as evidenced by concurrent drops in stride length (not tracked monthly but seen in recent runs: 66.6–75.9 m vs prior 77.6–83.6 m) and rising vertical oscillation (7.5–8.0% vs 5.5–6.6%).

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 49.3 km across 7 remaining sessions — ~7.0 km/session — but current readiness score is 38/100, resting HR is trending downward due to fatigue (not fitness), and sleep debt is severe (15/14 nights <7h). Chasing this number is unsafe and counterproductive; recovery, not volume, is the priority.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt directly degrades running economy
insights.body: Recent running economy median is 253.5 ml O2/kg/km — up from 234.6–253.9 in prior 5 runs — while sleep average remains 4.5h (15/14 nights <7h). Poor sleep impairs mitochondrial biogenesis and neuromuscular coordination, elevating oxygen cost even at same pace.

insights.title: ACWR of 0.6 reflects protective undertraining, not optimal taper
insights.body: Acute load (133) is just 62% of chronic load (216), far below the 0.8–1.3 'optimal' band. This isn’t peaking — it’s system-wide fatigue avoidance, confirmed by training readiness avg 7d = 34.9 and recovery balance (2.55) being driven by plummeting load, not rising HRV.

insights.title: Cadence surge masks deteriorating stride mechanics
insights.body: Cadence rose from 118 to 152 spm, yet vertical oscillation increased from 5.5–6.6% to 7.5–8.0%, ground contact time stayed elevated (298–307ms), and stride length dropped (e.g., 66.6m on 2026-08-02 vs 79.5m on 2026-07-31) — indicating inefficient, compensatory shuffling rather than efficient turnover.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling is improving (4.8%) but remains volatile
insights.body: Latest decoupling is 4.8% (within target), yet recent median is 7.11% and values swing from 0.84% to 9.37% — suggesting inconsistent aerobic resilience tied to variable recovery (HRV delta = -0.2, sleep debt persistent). Stability requires sleep consistency first.

recommendations.action: Prioritize 7+ hours of sleep for 5 consecutive nights — use Body Battery and resting HR trends to confirm recovery before resuming structured work
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt is the strongest modifiable driver of HRV suppression, VO2max stagnation, and economy decline; current 4.5h avg prevents autonomic rebound

recommendations.action: One 30-min Zone 1 walk or easy spin (HR <115 bpm) on Tuesday and Thursday — zero running, no pace or distance targets
recommendations.reason: Maintains neuromuscular priming without cardiovascular or orthopedic load; supports parasympathetic re-engagement during compromised readiness

recommendations.action: Skip all Zone 3+ efforts until resting HR stabilizes ≥51 bpm AND 7-day training readiness avg ≥55
recommendations.reason: Current avg resting HR (50.5 bpm) and readiness (34.9) indicate systemic fatigue — Zone 3+ work risks reinforcing inefficient motor patterns and delaying aerobic recovery

risk_flags.risk: Chronic sleep deprivation impairing metabolic recovery
risk_flags.evidence: 15 nights <7h sleep in last 14 days; HRV baseline unchanged (64.3 → 64.1 ms); VO2max plateaued (recent avg 39.1 vs baseline 37.1, +5.2% but no further gain)
risk_flags.action: Implement strict sleep hygiene protocol: lights out by 22:00, no screens after 21:00, consistent wake time

risk_flags.risk: Compensatory gait mechanics increasing injury risk
risk_flags.evidence: Vertical oscillation increased to 7.5–8.0% (vs 5.5–6.6% earlier), ground contact time remains >298ms despite higher cadence, stride length dropped up to 12.9m (79.5 → 66.6)
risk_flags.action: Replace all running with non-impact movement (pool walk, cycling) until vertical oscillation normalizes to ≤6.5% for 3 consecutive sessions

weekly_focus.description: Shift emphasis from output (km, pace, zones) to input regulation: restoring sleep architecture, lowering sympathetic tone via HR-guided movement, and halting compensatory biomechanics before they become ingrained.
suggested_sessions: 10-min diaphragmatic breathing + HRV biofeedback (target HRV ≥68 ms)
Foam roll quads/IT band + calf release (15 min, no running)
